_about: Approved by Nav on 2026-11-19 (phase 7a). The daily crew vote's pool. Each day the server picks one 'faster', one 'steady' and one 'detour' option, avoiding the last 3 days' picks. hours: the effect on the arrival date (negative = sooner), applied to the route at coasting speed. Detours carry a true fact for the mission log; every fact must be checked against its source before launch (Product principle 5). A tie goes to the steady option.

options.label: Detour for a photo of Earth and the Moon together: about a day later
options.result: Arrival about a day later.
options.fact: The Moon is a little over a quarter of Earth's width: about 3,475 km across, against Earth's 12,742 km.

options.label: Turn the camera on Venus: about 12 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 12 hours later.
options.fact: Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System, hotter even than Mercury: its surface is about 465 °C.

options.label: Swing by a passing asteroid for a close-up: about 18 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 18 hours later.
options.fact: Most known asteroids orbit the Sun in the main belt, between Mars and Jupiter.

options.label: Photograph Jupiter from afar: about 6 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 6 hours later.
options.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together.

options.label: Stop to measure the solar wind: about 8 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 8 hours later.
options.fact: The solar wind streams out from the Sun at around 400 km a second, about 20 times faster than our probe coasts.

options.label: Point the telescope at the moons of Mars: about 12 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 12 hours later.
options.fact: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos. Phobos, the bigger one, is only about 22 km across.

options.label: Zoom in on Olympus Mons: about 10 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 10 hours later.
options.fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the Solar System, about 22 km high: two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.

options.label: Fly along the dust trail of an old comet: about 8 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 8 hours later.
options.fact: Meteor showers happen when Earth passes through the trail of dust a comet leaves behind.

options.label: Photograph the Milky Way with no air in the way: about 6 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 6 hours later.
options.fact: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, holds an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars.

options.label: Take a long look back at Earth: about 12 hours later
options.result: Arrival about 12 hours later.
options.fact: Earth and Mars come closest about every 26 months, which is why Mars missions launch in windows that far apart.
